requirements.title: Staff permissions are role based
requirements.note: M1.4 delivers the role/permission catalog, scoped effective-dated staff assignments, and the central deny-by-default authorization service (ADR-0005). M1.5 connects it to routes, objects, fields, scoped queries, files, and noninteractive contracts (ADR-0011); real scope adapters arrive in M2 and the exhaustive matrix in M1.7. M1.7: every role × permission pair (9 × 167) and every scope type is proven at policy level against the accepted catalog with drift control; real M2 scope resolvers remain synthetic, so this stays partial. M2.1: organization, branch, and team scopes now resolve through the real organization adapter; assigned-record and audit-assignment scopes remain unresolved until their entities exist.

requirements.title: Recent authentication for sensitive actions
requirements.note: M1.3 delivers the server-owned recent-authentication primitive (named policies, purpose binding, /staff/reauthenticate) and applies it to staff password change and backup-code regeneration. Business high-risk actions adopt it in their own work items; candidate step-up is not configured. M1.4 composes the primitive into permission-level named recent-auth requirements (purpose-bound, strong methods, no reuse across privilege expansion); route adoption is M1.5. M1.7: every configured recent-authentication policy/purpose in the catalog is proven at exact controlled-clock boundaries (strength, purpose, session, account version, privilege-expansion floor); business commands that use them arrive in M2+.

requirements.title: Authentication events are auditable
requirements.note: M1.6 (ADR-0012): every M1 authentication, recovery, MFA, session, account, role/scope, catalog, restricted-access, and high-risk authorization-denial event is registered in the versioned audit catalog and persisted durably to the append-only, HMAC-chained audit_event or security_event stream (approved routine telemetry stays log-only). App-owned changes append atomically in the same transaction; Better Auth-committed changes are recorded right after the provider commit and success is withheld if recording fails (documented PROVIDER_COMMITTED limitation, ADR-0012 §5).
